topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by introducing the speaker, the course framework, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Genetic, Evolutionary, and Endogenous Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous mutational processes, microenvironmental factors, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Epidemiology, and the Cancer Etiology Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental carcinogen exposures, geographic variations in incidence, and the debate surrounding the relative contribution of intrinsic mutations versus external risk factors.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the role of infectious pathogens in cancer development, using Epstein-Barr virus and Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate mechanisms of viral oncogenesis.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Xenobiotic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental radiation and chemical agents undergo metabolic processing to produce reactive intermediates, oxidative stress, and DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Carcinogenesis Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe non-mutagenic promotional mechanisms driven by inflammation and signaling, tissue and developmental vulnerabilities, and conclude with a summary of carcinogenic pathways.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect and prove the carcinogenic potential of various agents.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing environmental exposure management within everyday risk-benefit decisions.
